page.layout: Running head at top centre with the page number at the top left. Two woodcut medallions with legends across the top of the text block, no printed text in them except their legends. Below them, one column of running text in two paragraphs, full width. No notes in the margins.

main_text.p: CYRVS Perfarũ Rex primus, imperauit apud Perfas anno mundi 3403. ante Christũ natum 559. rexitque annos 30. hic filius fuit Cambyfæ, & Mandanes, quæ filia erat Astyagis Medorum Regis. A filiis pastorum, Rex appellatus est per ludum, cum esset annorũ 12. Nam iusserat eum occidi Astyages, ob somnium, quòd viderat ex genitalibus filiæ vitem enasci, quæ totam Asiam occuparet: attamen ab vxore Mitradatis, seruatus & enutritus est, cui vxori nomen erat Cyno, quod Græcè canem significat. hic consilio Harpagi aduersus Astyagem exercitũ duxit, eúmq; superauit prodente Harpago, vlciscente mortem filij, quem in e[?]ulium[?] paratum, ei edendum dederat Astyages, ob seruatum Cyrum. Cum Cyro regnauit Cyaxares Astyagis filius apud Medos, anno 20. antequam Cyrus Babyloniam caperet, vt ait Xenophon lib.8. Cyrus iste à Daniele vocatur Darius, item ab Esdras, 3.Esdræ 3. De Cyro vide Herodo. lib.1. & Iustin.lib.item 1.Oro.lib.2.cap.6. & 7.

TOMYRIS, regina Massagetarum in Scythia, cum Cyro pugnauit, vicit, omnémque eius exercitum internecioni dedit: erant autem militum 20000. Sic vlta est filij mortem, quem Cyrus per bellicas insidias cum suis interfecerat: nã amisso hęc exercitu quem præmiserat, & vnico filio, orbitatis dolore non in lachrymas effudit, sed in vltionis solatia intendit: hostésque recenti victoria exultantes, pari insidiarum fraude circûdedit: quippe simulata diffidentia, Cyrum vsq; ad angustias perduxit: ibi compositis in montibus insidiis, exercitum cum Rege trucidauit, neq; nuncius tantæ cladis vllus superfuit. Cyri caput in vtrem demisit, quem humano cruore cõpleuerat, cum hac exprobratione crudelitatis, Satia te sanguine(inquit)quem sitisti. Herod.li.1. Iust.li.1. acta sunt an.mun.3432. ante Christũ natum 530.

page.notes: Two woodcut medallions above the text carry legends that are not transcribed. Left medallion, a bearded man: legend partly visible, reading roughly "CI" on the left and "RVS" on the right, probably CYRVS, with the rest unreadable. Right medallion, a helmeted female head in profile: legend around the rim reads "TOMYRIS" and "SCYTAR" on the left and "REGIN" on the right, probably SCYTARVM REGINA; the rim letters are not fully legible. The line "in e[?]ulium[?]" is doubtful: the letters between "e" and "ulium" are not clear. Words marked [?] are those whose letters were hard to read at this scan resolution.
